INTRODUCTION
 
            I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs having been authorised by the Committee to
submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this One-Hundred and Nineteenth Report on the Demands for Grants (2006-2007) relating to the
Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
2.         Under Rule 272 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Council of States, during the Budget Session after the general discussion
on the Budget in the Houses is over and the Houses are adjourned for a fixed period, the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees are
mandated to consider the Demands for Grants of the related Ministries during the said recess period of Parliament and make reports thereon to the Houses
within the specific period.  But in view of the rescheduling of the Budget Session (2006), a decision was taken to conclude the entire financial business
before the Houses adjourned for the Budget recess and Rule 272 was suspended in its application to consideration of Demands for Grants (2006-07) of the
related Ministries/Departments by Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees, by a Motion moved by the Minister of State in the Ministry of
Parliamentary Affairs in the Rajya Sabha on March 18, 2006 which was adopted by the House on the same day.  Notwithstanding discussion and voting
on the Demands for Grants of the respective Ministries/Departments for the year 2006-07 by the Lok Sabha, during the first part of the Budget Session, it
was decided by the Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha and Hon’ble Speaker, Lok Sabha that the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees
will examine the Demands for Grants and present their reports thereon to the respective Houses.

REPORT
 
CHAPTER-I
OVERVIEW
 
Maintenance of internal security in the country is the primary responsibility of the Ministry of Home Affairs.  In addition, the Ministry also has the
following broad responsibilities:
Issue of Notification in respect of Appointment of President/Vice-President, Prime Minister and Members of the Union Council of Ministers;
Appointment of Governors and Lt. Governors;
Regulation of Pay and Allowances of the Ministers;
Carrying out Census in India once every ten years;
Management of the International Borders;
Management and Deployment of the Central Police Forces;
Centre-States Relations/Inter-State Relations;
Administration of Union Territories;
Implementation of the Provisions of the Official Language Act, 1963;
Maintenance of Communal Harmony and Promotion of National Integration;
Co-ordination of Policy Relating to Human Rights;
Providing Relief and Rehabilitation to Refugees/Displaced Persons;
Regulation of Entry of Foreigners into India;
Grant of Pension and Other Benefits to Freedom  Fighters;
Prevention and Combat of Drug Abuse and Drug Trafficking;
Formulation and implementation of National Disaster Management Programme; and
Border Area Development Programme.
 
2.         To discharge the above responsibilities, the Ministry has been divided into following six constituent Departments:
(i)         Department of Internal Security;
Department of States;
Department of Official Language;
(iv)       Department of Home;
Department of Jammu and Kashmir Affairs; and
(vi)       Department of Border Management.
 
2.1       The Department of Internal Security deals with Police, Law and Order and Rehabilitation; Department of States deals with Centre-State relations,
inter-State relations, Union Territories and Freedom Fighters’ Pension; Department of Official Language is concerned with the implementation of the
provisions of the Constitution relating to Official Language and provisions of the Official Language Act, 1963; Department of Home deals with
notification relating to assumption of office by the President and Vice-President, notification of appointment of the Prime Minister and other Ministers,
etc;  Department of Jammu and Kashmir Affairs deals with all constitutional provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir and all other
matters relating to the State of Jammu and Kashmir excluding those with which the Ministry of External Affairs is concerned; Department of Border
Management deals with management of international borders including coastal borders. 
           
2.2       The Ministry is under the overall charge of Home Minister assisted by three Ministers of State. All Departments of the Ministry except the
Department of Official Language are interlinked and are headed by the Home Secretary who is assisted by Secretary (Border Management), one Special
Secretary, three Additional Secretaries and nineteen Joint Secretaries. The Department of Official Language has a separate Secretary and functions
independently.  The Ministry is further divided into eighteen divisions for administrative purposes and are concerned with the tasks mentioned below for
each division:-
 
(i)         Centre State Division
The Division deals with Central-State relations, including working of the Constitutional provisions governing such relations; appointment of Governors;

The Division deals with matters relating to internal security, including anti-national and subversive activities of various groups/extremist organizations. 
 
(iii)       Police Division
The Division functions as the cadre controlling authority of IPS officers and also deals with all matters relating to Central Police Forces, including their

(iv)       Union Territories  Division
The Division deals with all legislative and constitutional matters relating to Union Territories including Delhi and Pondicherry.  It also functions as the

Service (DANICS)/ Delhi Andaman Nicobar Islands Police Service (DANIPS).  It is also responsible for overseeing the crime situation in UTs.
 
(v)        North-Eastern Division
The Division deals with the law and order situation in North-Eastern States, including matters relating to insurgency and talks with various extremist
groups operating in that region.
 
(vi)       Jammu & Kashmir  Division
The Division deals with the Constitutional matters including Article 370 and general policy matters in respect of J&K and terrorism/militancy in that
State; it is also responsible for implementation of the PM’s Package for J&K.
 
(vii)      Foreigners Division
The Division deals with all matters relating to Foreigners Act,1946; Passport (Entry into India) Act,1920; Registration of Foreigners Act,1939; the
Citizenship Act,1955 and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act,1976.  It also controls Bureau of Immigration.
 
(viii)      Freedom Fighters & Rehabilitation Division
The Division frames and implements the Freedom Fighters Pension Scheme and the schemes for rehabilitation of migrants from former West
Pakistan/East Pakistan and provision of relief to Srilankan and Tibetan refugees.
 
(ix)       Human Rights Division
The Division deals with matters relating to the Protection of Human Rights Act and also matters relating to national integration and Ayodhya Affairs.
 
(x)        Disaster Management Division
The newly created Division is responsible for coordination of relief measures in the event of natural calamities and man-made disasters (except drought
and epidemics).
 
(xi)       Border Management Division
This Division deals with all matters relating to management of international borders.
 
(xii)      Police Modernization Division
The Division handles all items of work relating to modernisation of State Police Forces, provisioning/procurement of various items for modernisation of
Central Police Forces, police reforms, police training and VIP/Installation Security.
 
(xiii)      Policy Planning Division
It deals with matters relating to policy formulation in respect of counter-terrorism, international covenants, bilateral assistance treaties and related items of
work.
 
(xiv)     Finance Division
The Division is responsible for formulating, operating and controlling the budget of the Ministry under the Integrated Finance Scheme.
 
(xv)      Security Division
The Division deals with arms and explosives, narcotics, coastal security, National Security Act,1980.
 
(xvi)     Judicial Division
The Division deals with all matters relating to the legislative aspects of the IPC/Cr PC and the Commissions of Inquiry Act.1952; it also handles matters
relating to the State legislations to the extent such legislation require the assent of the President under the Constitution.
 
(xvii)     Administration Division
The Division is responsible for handling all administrative matters of the Ministry of Home Affairs and it also deals with matters relating to Table of
Precedence, Padma Awards, Flag Code, Prevention of Insult to National Honour Act and Secretariat Security Organisation.
 
(xviii)   Coordination Division
The division deals with intra-Ministry coordination work, Parliamentary matters, public grievances, monitoring of compliance of furnishing information
under the Right to Information Act, 2005, etc.

DEMAND NUMBERS 94, 95, 96, 97, AND 98  – UNION TERRITORIES (WITHOUT LEGISLATURE)
 
6.6.0    Though the budget of the Union Territories without legislature forms part of Ministry of Home Affairs, being the nodal Ministry, it, however, does
not dilute the responsibilities of the other Ministries of the Central Government from scrutinising and sanctioning the schemes under their purview. The
factual position regarding budgetary procedure in this regard is that the entire budget requirement for Plan and Non-Plan, revised estimates for current
year and Non-Plan budget estimates for the ensuing year is discussed by the Ministry of Finance in the pre-budget meetings with the representatives of the

Revamping of Civil Defence
8.0       Civil Defence is an important aspect of the country’s internal defence system. In accordance with the Civil Defence Act, 1960, Civil Defence
Corps have been established in the States. National Civil Defence College, Nagpur does the task of professionally training volunteers for Civil Defence. 
The Home Ministry, besides maintaining this institution, has been reimbursing State Governments, in the form of grants-in-aid, some part of the

Modernization of Fire Services
 
9.0       Preservation of life and property of the people being the States’ responsibility, the State Governments maintain fire services for its prevention and
fighting.  The Ministry of Home Affairs renders technical advice to States/UTs and Central Ministries on Fire Protection, Fire Prevention and Fire
Legislation.  The Government had drawn up a scheme in 2005-06 for Modernisation of Fire Services in the states for a period of five years starting from
2005-06. The scheme was finalised in consultation with the State Governments. The scheme envisaged that the Fire Services would be strengthened by
adding 1856 numbers of fire stations, upgrading existing training centres in stages, providing upgraded versions of water tenders, resume tenders, etc to
augment the existing fleet. A provision of Rs. 134.26 crore was made in BE 2005-06 for Grants-in-aid to States for ‘Modernization of Fire Services’.
However, there was no allocation reflected in RE 2005-06. Similarly only a token provision of Rs. 1 lakh have been made in BE 2006-07 for the purpose
on the ground that modalities of the scheme could not be finalized.
 
9.1       In response to a query of the Committee about the reasons for delay in finalizing the modalities for such an important and critical scheme, the
Ministry stated that an amount of Rs. 134.26 crore in BE 2005-06 was initially provided on Non-Plan side for the scheme for “Modernisation of Fire
Services”. However, at the appraisal and scrutiny stage, the Ministry of Finance advised them that it would be more appropriate to take up the scheme on
Plan side.  Accordingly, the Ministry requested the Planning Commission to provide necessary funds on Plan side to take up the scheme.  The Ministry
further stated that pending adequate provision of funds, a token provision of Rs. 1 lakh was made in BE 2006-07, and action for implementation of the
project would be initiated as soon as funds on the Plan side were provided and project approvals obtained. Clarifying the position further, the AS & FA in
his oral submission stated that last year they had prepared the proposal.  The process of approaching Planning Commission took away a lot of time. The
Home Secretary added that the entire exercise was in progress in consultation with State Governments and NDMA. The Home Secretary also stated that
they intended to come out with the scheme very soon and hence the token provision,
 
9.2       The Committee regrets that as in the case of the scheme of Revamping of Civil Defence, the scheme of Modernisation of Fire Services too could
not take off last year inspite of a provision of Rs. 134.26 crore in BE 2005-06. The Committee takes a serious view of the fact that new schemes are
initiated, allocations are made and they do not take off due to procedural and administrative delays. Although fire services in the country are primarily the
responsibility of the States/Municipal Committees/ Corporations, the services across the country are abysmally below the International Standards. The
Committee desires that Modernisation of Fire services which is a comprehensive scheme should be equipped with modern technology, gadgets and
infrastructure.  The Committee while expressing concern over delay of one year in implementing the scheme urges upon the Government to get the
scheme cleared in a definite time frame from NDMA and Planning Commission and make necessary allocation at RE 2006-07 stage. The Committee also
urges upon the Ministry to implement the scheme during the current fiscal year.

that all efforts made in this regard by Delhi Police have failed to bring substantial change in the situation.  It is legally as well as morally binding upon the
law enforcement agency to make sincere efforts in nabbing the perpetrators of crime against women and see to it that punishment is handed down in such
a way as to set an example to deter potential offenders.  The Committee is of the view that the lackluster style of functioning of the police force is greatly
responsible for not instilling a sense of security and confidence amongst the women in Delhi. The Committee, therefore, recommends that adequate
women police personnel should be deployed in police stations and at other places considered vulnerable for women. Investigation of cases of crime
against women should be completed within a definite time frame so that conviction of the delinquent is secured without losing time. The Committee also
recommends that Delhi Police should launch a drive to educate women in self-defence through posters and pamphlets and also launch awareness
campaigns amongst women about their proactive approach in dealing with the cases of atrocities committed against them.   The Committee further
recommends that Delhi Police should address this issue with utmost sincerity and honesty by adopting all necessary measures.       
                                                                   (para 17.10.0)
 
The Committee is also given to understand that a large number of women are working in Call Centers in NCR and travel long distance from their
place of residence to their place of work at odd hours.  Cases of rapes and atrocities on such women employees have been reported from certain places. 
The Committee, therefore, desires that Delhi Police should take all precautionary measures to ensure that such incidents do not happen in NCT of Delhi.
The Committee also feels that there is a need for gender sensitization among Delhi Police personnel and all efforts may be made for ensuring attitudinal
change amongst Delhi Police personnel.             (para 17.10.1)
 
Housing
 
The Committee feels that proper housing facilities for police personnel particularly at the level of Constable and Head Constable will go a long
way in improving their efficiency particularly their attitude and behaviour.  The Committee expresses its deep anguish over the laxity shown by Delhi
Police in improving the satisfaction level in the housing of Delhi Police personnel particularly at lower level.  Inspite of serious concern expressed by the
Committee in the earlier years and recommendations made for improvement, there is no perceptible change in the situation.  Housing is one of the basic
requirements, particularly for people working in an organisation like Delhi Police and it should be made available to the extent possible.  The Committee
also expresses its concern that inspite of facing problem from several fronts in meeting the housing requirement they have not been able to set up the Delhi
Police Housing Corporation.  Housing Corporation will be an important step in the direction of solving the problem and the Committee strongly
recommends that it may be established during the current financial year. The allocation made for housing in the current year i.e. Rs.55 crore may be fully
utilized in the construction and purchase of housing units.  The Committee is happy to learn that Rs. 100 crore are going to be made available every year
for housing of Delhi Police personnel from out of the new scheme likely to be launched i.e. Modernisation of Police Forces in UTs.  The allocation could
not be made for this scheme at BE 2006-07 due to procedural delay and the Committee has already made its observation in para 16.4 supra.            Since
the scheme has already been approved, the Committee desires that allocation may be made for the scheme and Delhi Police may finalise its proposal for
utilisation  of the amount likely to be made available to it.                                                                                                                                 (para 17.14)
